expectations.text: Does NOT simply validate the colleague's claim that alpha = .83 at both time points means the change score is reliable

expectations.text: Explains that difference score reliability depends on both the component reliabilities AND the pre-post correlation — it is not simply inherited from the components
expectations.evidence: No mention of the pre-post correlation's role in change score reliability. The response discusses only alpha at each time point without introducing the difference score reliability formula or the r_xy dependency.

expectations.text: States the direction of the effect: as the pre-post correlation rises (which it typically does in intervention studies), difference score reliability falls — often dramatically
expectations.evidence: The response is silent on the pre-post correlation entirely. It never identifies r_xy as a threat to reliability and never describes the direction of the effect.

expectations.text: Provides a concrete illustration: with alpha = .83 and a typical pre-post correlation of, say, r = .70, change score reliability falls to roughly .43 — well below acceptable thresholds

expectations.text: Names at least one preferred alternative: ANCOVA on post-scores (controls for baseline without subtracting it) or latent change score model in SEM
